content.text: Does runregression batch compile? So if I give it 4 workers, it will comile in batches of 4?
I’ll check how `runregression` uses its worker count. I’m using the directory structure and testing skills to locate the relevant code.

input.input: text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"sed -n '1155,1193p' gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua; sed -n '1228,1272p' gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua; sed -n '1990,2028p' gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua; sed -n '2047,2056p' gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua; rg -n 'run_action|run_regression|runRegression|function.*run|return.*run' gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua","max_output_tokens":3200}));

content.text:
Yes—in the current source, `--jobs 4` compiles **up to four C regression tests concurrently**, each using `make -j1`.

It uses a rolling worker pool: whenever one finishes, the next starts immediately, without waiting for all four. All compilation finishes before test execution begins.

For compilation only:

```sh
gkeyll runregression run -c -j 4 compile
```

See the [compilation pool](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua:1159) and [worker scheduling](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gkeyll/lua/Tool/runregression.lua:1252).
